data.revised_prompt: The four circular motor mounts at the ends of the diagonal bars in <Picture 1> are <Subject 1>. The light neutral background and centered framing in <Picture 1> are <Subject 2>. The target image is a strict orthographic top-view industrial design rendering of a compact X-layout quadcopter on <Subject 2>, keeping <Subject 1> in place while replacing the flat grey bars with three-dimensional dark graphite arms, a matte light grey spindle-shaped fuselage, and unfolded two-blade propellers. <Subject 1> is partially preserved; its exact positions, scale, and spacing remain unchanged, while its flat grey circles become realistic cylindrical motor bells with central mounting nuts and subtle metallic shading. <Subject 2> is fully preserved. Replacing the flat intersecting bars from <Picture 1>, four slender dark graphite arms run diagonally from the center to <Subject 1>, tapering outward and merging smoothly into the sides of the central body through long, seamless tapered blends without joint lines. At the center, a slender spindle-shaped fuselage oriented vertically with its nose toward the top edge features a matte light grey top shell about 2.6 times as long as wide, occupying less than a quarter of the distance between opposite motors. A single clean lengthwise seam runs down the center of the smooth, vent-free top shell, which narrows at the top into a small rounded tip enclosing a forward-facing camera pod whose lens points straight ahead and remains hidden beneath the nose profile. Each of the four motors at <Subject 1> carries one fully unfolded, symmetrical two-blade dark graphite propeller with equal-length blades resting cleanly over the arm roots. Soft, even studio lighting creates gentle gradients across the curved matte light grey shell and dark graphite components, clearly defining their three-dimensional volume against <Subject 2> with no text, markings, or accent colors.
